attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in his signed post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with a decade horizon; 'maybe much less' hedges only the timing. The normalised text drops 'a wide range of', which narrows the claim. The contract restores it in its explicit elements.

contract.note: Reading 'pure focus' as the dominant emphasis, plus a field-wide shift standard, is an ordinary and fair plain reading. The deadline of 2032-12-25 matches the stated decade.

evidence.note: Company disclosure from 2024 describing augmented LLMs. It is one vendor's example, not a measure of the field's focus.
The 2020 RAG paper predates the forecast. It is background on the starting point, not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2032-12-25, after the evaluation date. The packet has only isolated examples of integration and no representative field-wide comparison, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The forecast is not yet scoreable.

semantics.note: 'Guarantee' is a firm forecast. The context ties it to GPT-4's release, and the normalised text preserves this.

contract.note: Strongly impressed reactions from multiple users at launch is a fair, ordinary reading. It does not require universal amazement.

evidence.note: OpenAI's disclosure establishes the release on 2023-03-14. It shows the condition was met, not the reception.
A launch-day report quotes a named early user saying they were 'absolutely blown away'. He had a commercial interest.
TIME quotes a cardiologist who found GPT-4 very impressive after testing it, plus other strongly impressed users.
A restrained contemporary assessment ('incremental'). It limits any claim of universal amazement but does not negate the impressed reactions.

reviews.rationale: GPT-4 was released in March 2023. Multiple named users in independent outlets reported being strongly impressed at launch, which meets the early-resolution rule. Restrained views existed but do not show that ordinary reactions predominated.

attribution.note: One of Marcus's own seven predictions.

semantics.note: A firm 'will still be unreliable' about GPT-4 across three domains. The GPT-3 clause is background and is rightly not graded.

contract.note: Reading 'unreliable' as recurring failures despite substantial competence is fair and ordinary. Requiring all three domains is appropriately strict.

evidence.note: NEWTON (2023) found uneven physical reasoning, with a scenario where GPT-4 was inconsistent. GPT-4's high overall scores make this the weakest of the three domains.
GPT-4-0314 scored near-perfectly on standard false-belief tasks but 0% on some altered theory-of-mind variants, showing it is not robust.
GSM-Plus (2024): GPT-4's correct answers on original maths problems did not reliably transfer to controlled variations.
Peer-reviewed study finding GPT-4 at or above human level on many theory-of-mind tests, with its faux-pas weakness attributed to caution. This is counterweight.

reviews.rationale: Original evaluations document recurring GPT-4 robustness failures in physical, theory-of-mind and mathematical reasoning, which meets the early-resolution rule. Counterevidence shows substantial competence, not consistently dependable reasoning. The physical evidence is the thinnest.

semantics.note: A firm 'will remain difficult to anticipate'. The normalised text keeps the core claim; the 'often/sometimes' framing is implicit.

contract.note: Operationalising this as users' advance expectations versus GPT-4's actual correctness is a fair, ordinary reading. It narrows 'what you want' to correctness.

evidence.note: A 2024 study estimated human beliefs from about 19,000 responses: GPT-4 did best at equal weighting but worst in high-stakes settings, i.e. users were overconfident. Beliefs were modelled, not directly elicited.

reviews.rationale: One empirical study shows GPT-4 succeeding frequently alongside consequential gaps between human expectations and its actual correctness, which meets the early-resolution rule. Limits: a single preprint, estimated rather than observed beliefs, and correctness only.
